{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVaC1p88AAAABa2UW-A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BpEKozhEcGWs", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BpEKo", "number": 20, "title": "Render a CPU-programmed BG1 tile using VRAM in the browser", "body": "## Problem

WebRTL already runs a real P65C816 RTL CPU and a small PPU backdrop example (#18), but the PPU currently renders only a solid CGRAM color. To progress toward an SNES hardware demo, the next focused step is **CPU-programmed VRAM and a visible BG1 tile**, reusing the existing browser-only compiler and Video/Canvas path.

## Expected outcome

Add a small, synthesizable **SNES-inspired BG1 Mode 0 (2bpp) tile-rendering** example. A freely redistributable 65C816 test ROM writes palette, tile graphics and tilemap data through **memory-mapped PPU registers**. The RTL PPU reads those memories and emits a deterministic 64×48 frame whose visible pattern depends on those CPU writes.

This is a real CPU → PPU-registers → VRAM/CGRAM → BG1 pixels pipeline, **not** a JavaScript-rendered pattern or prerecorded image.

## Implementation scope

- Extend the existing backdrop example or add a closely related example reusing its pinned GPL-3.0-or-later P65C816 core, CPU bus integration, scanout adapter and license/provenance.
- Implement the minimum documented PPU register subset needed for CPU VRAM and BG1 programming: relevant portions of `$2105` (BGMODE), `$2107` (BG1SC), `$210B` (BG12NBA), `$2115` (VMAIN), `$2116/$2117` (VMADD), `$2118/$2119` (VMDATA), plus existing `$2100` and `$2121/$2122` (CGRAM). Clearly document which bits and write/increment semantics are supported and which are omitted.
- Store enough **RTL-owned VRAM** for at least one 8×8, 2bpp BG1 character and tilemap entry(s). Implement the relevant planar tile-byte interpretation, tilemap lookup, and palette index selection. Support CGRAM entries required for the test's transparent/backdrop and nonzero tile pixels; avoid pretending the prior single-backdrop-entry CGRAM subset is sufficient.
- Supply an **original permitted machine-code ROM** that blanks the display, initializes CGRAM and VRAM through CPU register writes, configures the BG1 display subset and unblanks it. Use a visibly nonuniform pattern (e.g. stripes or checkerboard), not a solid color. Keep the ROM small and reproducible; direct JS writes to VRAM/PPU state do not count.
- Keep the existing browser video signal contract and 64×48 Canvas output. Document simulation clocks, frame-boundary behavior, reset and the supported SNES register subset. Prefer a deliberately small VRAM/tilemap implementation over an unnecessary full PPU.
- Make the example selectable in the existing multi-file browser project UI; preserve the current counter, CPU bus, 65C816, backdrop, video and audio examples.
- Record compiler size/time and active-model throughput for the example; avoid raising limits unless necessary, with justification and regression coverage.

## Out of scope

- Full SNES PPU, all BG modes/layers, scrolling, sprites/OAM, Mode 7, color math, windows, DMA/HDMA, interrupts, real NTSC timing, cartridge mappers, game ROM loading or a complete console.
- Generic video/GPU rendering frameworks, a new HDL compiler, or custom JavaScript tile interpretation.
- Real-time SNES/game performance guarantees and human-only validation gates.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] The multi-file CPU + minimal BG1 RTL example compiles through the **existing client-side Yosys/CXXRTL/Clang → WASM** pipeline at the GitHub Pages-compatible `/webrtl/` path; no remote compilation API.
- [ ] Automated browser tests show the **actual 65C816** fetching the test program and writing the documented VRAM/PPU/CGRAM register sequence, with meaningful bus observations.
- [ ] A completed Canvas frame contains a **nonuniform 8×8-based tile pattern** derived from RTL VRAM/tilemap/palette logic and matches independently specified expected pixel values.
- [ ] Editing tile bytes, tilemap selection, or relevant palette bytes in the ROM and recompiling changes the expected pixels. Tests must rule out static/precomputed JS graphics and confirm the changed circuit is the source of truth.
- [ ] Reset and recompilation clear VRAM/PPU/scanout state deterministically; Run/Pause/Step work without stale frames. Forced blank and the existing backdrop behavior continue to work.
- [ ] Appropriate automated browser regressions for existing examples pass, including the previously implemented CPU and video paths.
- [ ] README and a focused guide document the register subset, VRAM layout, 2bpp bitplane/tilemap interpretation, ROM instructions, expected frames, licensing, limits and measured performance.
- [ ] The implementation stays focused on one minimal BG1 tile path; no speculative SNES-wide abstractions.

## Optional validation

- Additional test patterns, more tiles or a slightly larger tilemap without changing the scope.
- Compare relevant register and tile semantics against a documented SNES PPU reference.

## Required post-merge verification

After deployment, run an **automated browser smoke test** against the public GitHub Pages site that compiles the example, renders the expected tile pattern, edits the ROM/palette to change the pixels, resets and repeats. Report actual results separately; publication is not a pre-merge gate.

## Related

- #3 — WebRTL project vision
- #16 — Real 65C816 CPU RTL
- #18 — CPU-to-PPU backdrop example
- #10 — Reusable video output

Follow-ups: BG1 map coverage and scrolling, more PPU functionality, controller/cartridge/ROM loading, APU integration, and performance profiling.
